fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents honestly distinguish production Node.js/TypeScript work from basic personal Python and limited Terraform editing. SQS, passenger-transport work and alternative observability tools are useful adjacent experience, not substitutes for Kafka, freight expertise or the advertised monitoring stack. Database tuning, live schema migrations and design/incident documentation remain unsubstantiated; the Express-to-NestJS migration must not be mistaken for a database migration. The letter would be stronger with a clear expression of interest in working mainly in Python, without asserting prior production Python experience.

issues: The backend migration and its meetup presentation are repeated across Professional Experience, Selected Projects and Additional Experience.
The long frontend inventory, school education, incomplete machine-learning course, driving licence and references dilute the backend targeting.
The strongest role-relevant evidence is present, but testing is mostly a tool inventory rather than a description of tests or delivery safeguards.
The Selected Projects heading and first project title are stranded at the bottom of page one, with their bullets on page two.

reasons: The single-column PDF extracts in sensible order, with intact text, standard headings and clear employment dates.
Strong matches include PostgreSQL, REST, AWS, Docker, GitHub Actions, testing and an exactly matching on-call cadence.
Python is explicitly basic and personal; FastAPI and professional Python experience are absent.
Node.js backend tenure may satisfy the comparable-language provision, but a strict Python screen could reject the application.
Query tuning and schema migrations are important missing must-have evidence; most absent specialist keywords cannot honestly be added from the supplied material.

issues: The opening and third paragraph repeat the same backend stack and delivery experience.
The one-week-in-six on-call cadence is repeated in the closing paragraph.
The long second-paragraph sentence combines service development, migration and public speaking; splitting it would improve readability.
The mobile LCP result is legitimate but less relevant than a backend reliability or API-performance example.
It acknowledges limited Python honestly but does not explicitly express enthusiasm for working mainly in Python.
The company-specific motivation is accurate but fairly broad; the carrier-event pipeline or queue-to-Kafka transition would provide a sharper connection using the candidate's real SQS experience.
strengths: Names Tessel, the Backend Engineer role and the Routing & Tracking team correctly.
Connects production ownership and on-call experience to the company's own-operate model.
Clearly separates production Node.js/TypeScript experience from personal Python use.
Uses concrete service examples, asynchronous processing and observability experience.
Avoids the earlier letter's outdated employer, agency-to-product motivation and learning-NestJS framing.

culture_used: Small teams that build and operate their own services

spacing_issues: CV page one ends with Selected Projects and the Express-to-NestJS project title, while all supporting bullets begin on page two.
CV page one is densely packed, whereas page two is only 45.8% filled and has a large empty lower area.
The CV's experience entries have little vertical separation, making the densely populated first page harder to scan.
issues: The CV's 10-point body text is readable but compact for this amount of content.
Keep the first selected project together on page two and rebalance the two pages, preferably by removing repeated or low-relevance material.
The cover letter has comfortable 11-point text, clear paragraph spacing and no visible clipping or overlap.

fluency_and_tone_issues: “At Älvgrind, I have built services including ... and contributed ... and later presented ...” is an overloaded sentence; separate the service examples, migration and presentation.
“improving an incremental backend migration” is awkward; “contributing to an incremental backend migration” is clearer.
“My recent work has focused on” immediately follows “with recent work,” creating avoidable repetition.
“connects with my experience supporting production services” is generic and repeats earlier claims rather than adding a distinct reason for choosing Tessel.

notes_facts_used: Four months as acting team lead in 2024, covering 1:1s and sprint planning without changing the formal employment title.
notes_facts_ignored: Apollo Server as the implementation behind the maintained GraphQL BFF.

evaluation.summary: The application is factually disciplined and presents credible transferable backend experience in Node.js, PostgreSQL, AWS, testing and production on-call support. It correctly limits Python to personal projects, qualifies Terraform proficiency and avoids inventing work-arrangement commitments. The main fit weaknesses are unproven query tuning and schema migrations, limited Python depth, and no Kafka or Kubernetes evidence. The CV would benefit from tighter backend prioritisation and removal of repeated material, while its stranded project heading and uneven page density need layout correction; the letter is relevant but repetitive.
